Reference / web/reply

web/reply#

Endpoint replies.

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

TextReply("ok")
TextReply(text: "no access", status: Status.forbidden)
JsonReply(value: user, headers: Headers(Header(name: "Cache-Control", value: "no-store")))
RedirectReply(location: "/notes", headers: Headers(SetCookie(name: "sid", value: token)))

Description#

Endpoint replies. Each one builds a std Response with the defaults of its kind and takes only what differs: status: and headers:. Content-Type and Content-Length belong to the reply; any other field comes in headers:

An endpoint that needs full control answers a Response itself: both are Responding.

object StreamReply#

object StreamReply does Responding

A body read while it is sent, such as a generated export: StreamReply(body: opening, media_type: "text/csv"). Content-Length is declared when the body knows its length; otherwise HTTP/1.1 sends the body in chunks.

StreamReply.StreamReply#

body as media_type with status and headers.

The response it makes.

object EventsReply#

object EventsReply does Responding

Server-sent events from a channel, as text/event-stream (#82):

let events is Channel<ServerEvent> = Channel(capacity: 16);
spawn clock.ticks(events.sending());
EventsReply(events.receiving())

The stream ends when the channel closes. The reply sends Cache-Control: no-cache and X-Accel-Buffering: no, so proxies pass each event on at once.

EventsReply.EventsReply#

EventsReply(events is Receiving<ServerEvent>, headers is Headers = Headers())

Sends each event received from events until it closes.

EventsReply.response#

response() is Response

The response it makes.

object FileReply#

object FileReply does Responding

One file from an endpoint, with validators, ranges and the Content-Type of its name (#82):

FileReply(request: request, root: reports, path: "2026/q3.pdf")

path is below root and "/"-separated. A missing file is 404, a path that would leave the root 400, and a conditional or range request is answered as http/static answers it.

FileReply.FileReply#

FileReply(request is WebRequest, root is FileRoot, path is string, headers is Headers = Headers())

The file at path below root, for request.

response() is Response

The response it makes.
